issues.claim: §2.7's crossing table, *beneath* (l. 2645-2653), bars every gate and tower from an under-deck strip and moves 'one the wall's law would place there ... a tower along the trace ...; a gate along its way, the trace passing through it there ... or along the trace where the way is laid after the gate and follows it'. Two places the wall's law fixes fit neither clause. (1) A river's water gate: the trace 'never crosses water except at a water gate where a river passes', its bank vertices named by `Gate.banks` (§4.4 S5a, l. 5963-5967). It has no way to move along (`way` null), and moving it along the trace leaves the river crossed ungated. (2) The tower at an anchor: g item 106 (a) puts 'a tower at each anchor' (§4.8 *Towers*; `Enceinte.anchors`), and smoothing never moves an anchor (§4.4 S5a (3)); moving the tower along the trace leaves the anchor bare. Both are reachable on a normal CITY site: a stage-2 ring laid after an S4 viaduct that spans a river can cross that river, or end on its bank, inside the viaduct's under-deck strip, because the pull treats only ramps, stairs, feet and an aqueduct's supports as impassable (*beneath*; §4.4 S5a *Trace* (2)). The same holds for an aqueduct at S6's end crossing S3's trace near an anchor: *over the band* keeps its strip clear of 'the trace's gates and towers', but S7 lays the towers later and moves only 'a tower its spacing would place in the strip'. One builder leaves the water gate and gatehouse under the deck (against 'no gate ... in the under-deck strip' and W6's premise); another bends the trace. At an anchor, one moves the tower off it (against item 106 (a)); another moves the anchor. §4.8's lead narrows the rule further: '(one the spacing or the gate law would place there moved clear of it)'. No bar runs either case.
issues.required_change: §2.7's crossing table, *beneath*, *No gate and no tower in the under-deck strip*: after '... (a village track, V07 §3.5a (4))' add '; a gate or tower whose place the trace fixes — a river's water gate (where the trace crosses the river, `Gate.banks`) and the tower at a stretch's anchor (`Enceinte.anchors`; item 106 (a): a tower at each anchor) — moves with the trace: the trace's crossing of the river, or its anchor on the barrier, is moved along the river or the barrier to the nearest point clear of the strip — a trace laid by the pull or cost field treating the river's water and the barrier's edge inside an under-deck strip as no crossing or anchor site, a stretch laid by neither bent locally there (by hand a fate named in `bend.wall.raisedCrossing`'s line)'. *Over the band*: 'its under-deck strip keeps clear of the trace's gates and towers' -> 'its under-deck strip keeps clear of the trace's gates, towers and anchors'. Pipeline end, §4.8's lead: '(one the spacing or the gate law would place there moved clear of it)' -> '(one the wall's law would place there moved clear of it, a water gate's river crossing or an anchor with it; §2.7's crossing table, *beneath*)'. Scope end, T110-2 (3) adds 'and a stage-2 ring whose boundary crosses the river under an S4 viaduct's span and, on a second run, is anchored on that river's bank inside its under-deck strip — the river crossing with its water gate, and the anchor with its tower, moved along the river clear of the strip, the trace laid to them, 0 gates or towers in the under-deck strip'. (The adjudicator may rule another outcome — for example, a water gate lawful under a span whose soffit clears its gatehouse, capped like the run — provided each case has one outcome, item 106 (a)'s tower at each anchor holds and a bar runs it.)

issues.claim: Cells of §2.7's crossing table name tests that never run their case. (1) W3·C3-C6 (l. 2700): a regeneration re-deriving a ring under a held raised way whose span fell, whose support was cleared or toppled, or whose `vault` span was breached. Each cell reads '*beneath* as read · T110-2 (6)', but T110-2 (6) (l. 18598-18607) regenerates only standing raised ways ((1)'s aqueduct and (3)'s viaduct, locked). The fallen-part readings run only on the epoch path (T110-2 (7), T-V6-47, through V06's cost field). So the generation path that reads `state` is never run: S5a's pull treating a `cleared` ring as open ground and a `ruined` aqueduct support as impassable (§4.4 S5a *Trace* (2)), and S10's band whole across a cleared footprint. A pull that ignores `state` passes every bar. (2) W7·C2 (l. 2704): its outcome includes 'V04 lays again an arch vault the old wall stood over · T110-2 (8), T-V6-47'. Neither T110-2 (8) (l. 18615-18618) nor T-V6-47's `wallToWay` clause has a `vault` span under the ring, and T-V4-63 runs the re-lay only for a hand delete. A `wallToWay` that leaves the chamber unlaid, or lays it under the ring road's corridor, passes every bar — exactly the case where the re-laid vault makes the strip impassable again and row (c)'s re-route must avoid it. Under R6-01's grading, a defined edge that no bar runs, so that a wrong build passes, is MAJOR.
issues.required_change: §13.2's T110-2 (6) adds: 'and (1)'s c15 fixture with its locked aqueduct's span over the band `ruined`, a support by the band `cleared` and a `vault` span over the trace breached by scripted `DeclineOp`s, regenerated (keep) — the ring re-derived on its old trace at its own top beneath the fallen span, the trace through the cleared ring as open ground and the band whole across its footprint, no chamber under the wall, every station, key, span and state of the aqueduct unchanged (§2.7's crossing table, W3·C3–C6)'. T110-2 (8) adds: 'with (3)'s viaduct holding a `vault` span under the ring — after `wallToWay` its arch vault laid again with the same id (V04 §3.5.4 (d)), the ring road crossing the under-deck strip clear of that span's strip (§2.7's way-and-channel table, row c; W7·C2)'.

issues.claim: §2.7's crossing table, W11·C2 (l. 2708), reads '*unchanged meeting*: the run (its band, towers, gates) removed, the raised way untouched; V04 lays again an arch vault the run stood over · T110-2 (4)'. T110-2 (4)'s delete case ('a hand `delete` of a run beneath a standing viaduct — the viaduct unchanged, no bend, the run back on its undo', l. 18574-18575) holds no `vault` span. The vault's re-lay on a delete is run by T-V4-63 ('the hand wall's delete laying it again with the same id'), which the cell does not name.

§2.7's support step (3) bounds a slid station by 'both neighbouring spans stay ≤ `raisedWays.structure.slideMaxFactor` × the band's upper bound' (l. 2541). Round 6's (M1) made the obstacle list just before it read 'an enceinte's band (`Enceinte.band`, or before S10 has built it the band beside the standing trace, its half-widths ...)' (l. 2537-2539). So the nearest 'band' is now the wall's band, which has half-widths and no upper bound. The bound meant is (1)'s `pierSpacingM` band (l. 2532), as V11 §2.8c's `slideMaxFactor` comment says ('× the `pierSpacingM` band's upper bound', V11 l. 717).
issues.required_change: §2.7's support step (3): '× the band's upper bound' -> '× the `pierSpacingM` band's upper bound ((1))'.
